name: Andrew Ogles
groups: Chair, Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection (House Committee on Homeland Security)
signature: Chairs the House Homeland cyber subcommittee; ran hearings on frontier AI models, Chinese open-weight AI and AI-driven cyberattacks; lost his Aug 2026 primary.

notable_quote.text: The same models that hunt for software flaws can, without the right safeguards, help a bad actor work through the hardest steps of building a biological weapon.

data_centers.summary: No public position found on whether to build, slow or condition data centers as of Sept 2026, even though Nashville, partly in his district, paused permits in July 2026. His only data center activity is a hearing on protecting them from Chinese cyberattacks.

evidence.title: Homeland Committee advisory: Ogles announces hearing on cyber threats to telecom networks, data centers and satellites
evidence.quote: Our adversaries are actively seeking to exploit vulnerabilities in the subsea cables that keep us connected, the data centers that power the cloud, and the satellites that serve as the backbone of military operations
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data centers as critical infrastructure to defend from China, but says nothing about siting, power bills or whether more should be built.

ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Ogles calls frontier AI models a weapon in the wrong hands, warns they could help build bioweapons, and sponsored bills banning federal facial recognition ID checks and biometric databases. But he frames AI mainly as an arms race with China, praised Trump's voluntary early-access framework, and says oversight is not about slowing innovation.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Ogles opens hearing on frontier AI models and the future of cybersecurity
evidence.quote: In the right hands, that is a powerful defensive advantage. In the wrong hands, it is a weapon.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the most advanced AI models as a serious national security danger, including bioweapon risk once safeguards are stripped out.

evidence.title: Ogles question to witnesses at the June 4, 2026 AI security hearing (Tech Policy Press transcript)
evidence.quote: When you think about a regulatory framework for AI, how do we regulate AI in such a way to protect the consumer, the public, but yet not hinder ourselves against this arms race that essentially is against China?
evidence.what_it_shows: He is open to some AI regulation but weighs it against beating China.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Ogles and Brecheen hearing with Anthropic, Google and Quantum Xchange
evidence.quote: This is not about slowing innovation. It is about making sure innovation strengthens the nation rather than exposing it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames congressional oversight of AI as pro-innovation, not as new mandates.

evidence.title: Cyberscoop: written statement announcing the frontier AI hearing
evidence.quote: AI is the America First mission of the future, and it is becoming our number one offensive and defensive weapon against cyber terrorists
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts AI as a strategic weapon to be advanced, a light-touch, race-with-China framing.

evidence.title: Homeland Republicans (Garbarino, Ogles, Brecheen) request Anthropic, Google, Quantum Xchange testimony after AI-assisted PRC cyber operation
evidence.what_it_shows: He used his subcommittee to probe a largely autonomous AI-enabled cyberattack, treating advanced AI misuse as a live homeland security risk.

evidence.title: H.R. 3782, bill to prohibit the federal government from using facial recognition for identity verification
evidence.what_it_shows: A specific guardrail on government use of AI surveillance.

evidence.title: H.R. 3693, bill to prohibit a federal database of biometric identity data on US citizens
evidence.what_it_shows: Another limit on government biometric and AI identification tools.

tech_regulation.summary: Leans toward targeted rules: he cosponsored the SCREEN Act requiring age checks on adult websites. He did not vote on the 2024 TikTok divestiture bill, and no broader Big Tech or Section 230 statements were found.

evidence.title: H.R. 1623, SCREEN Act (age verification for adult websites)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a specific online safety rule for kids.

evidence.title: Roll call 86 (Mar 13, 2024), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok): Ogles Not Voting
evidence.what_it_shows: He did not record a vote on the TikTok divestiture bill, so it adds no signal either way.

preemption.summary: No statement found on the 10-year state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order or the Mar 2026 White House preemption framework as of Sept 2026.

china_chips.summary: Hawkish on Chinese AI: he warns the world must not become dependent on Chinese open-weight models, backs a joint investigation into their spread, and wants American open-weight alternatives. No statement found on Nvidia chip sales or export controls specifically.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Ogles opens hearing on frontier AI models and the future of cybersecurity
evidence.quote: We cannot let the world grow dependent on Chinese AI the way it grew dependent on other Chinese technologies we are now scrambling to address.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats Chinese AI models as a strategic threat and wants a US strategy to counter them.

evidence.title: Cyberscoop: written statement announcing the frontier AI hearing
evidence.quote: Communist China is moving aggressively to control the technologies that will define the future of economic and military power, and few technologies are more consequential than artificial intelligence
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI competition with China as the central national security issue.

evidence.title: Homeland Committee release: Garbarino and Moolenaar announce joint investigation into PRC AI models (names Ogles's letters to Anthropic and Google)
evidence.what_it_shows: His subcommittee's work fed into a formal investigation of Chinese AI models, a hawkish posture on Chinese AI rather than on chip exports.

search_notes: About 14 searches (AI, data centers, Big Tech, chips/China, preemption, chatbot/deepfake, Nashville Zoo/TVA, OpenAI letter, Israel AI bill, Quiver releases) plus Wayback listings of ogles.house.gov and homeland.house.gov. Opened: Homeland Committee releases (Jun 4 2026 opener, Dec 17 2025 opener, Nov 26 2025 letter, Apr 23 and Apr 29 2026 releases, Jan 2026 Examiner op-ed, Nov 2025 chair announcement), the full Tech Policy Press transcript, Cyberscoop (May 13 and May 28 2026), govtrack roll call 86 CSV. Headline-only, not opened: BBC and others report he lost the Aug 6, 2026 GOP primary to Charlie Hatcher; VitalLaw (paywalled) reported Aug 3, 2026 that House cyber panel leaders sought a briefing on OpenAI's misbehaving models; Haaretz reported he shared an AI-made video of himself as a Crusader. He also sponsored H.R. 3303 America-Israel AI Cooperation Act (research cooperation, neutral). Nothing found on data center siting, ratepayers, preemption or chip export controls.

name: John W. Rose
signature: 2026 governor candidate who called data centers a local decision needing a state framework and blamed Chinese money for stirring opposition; longtime TikTok and kids-online-safety hawk; lost the Aug 2026 GOP primary and is leaving the House.

notable_quote.text: I think the state should lead in establishing a framework for looking at these [data centers], but I think ultimately you want it to be locally controlled

data_centers.summary: Build, with conditions. As a candidate for governor he said data centers should be a local decision with a state framework to help communities evaluate them, said he is not opposed to data centers, and warned that blanket opposition helps China. He did not propose ratepayer or water protections.

evidence.title: Williamson Scene: Rose fields questions at Spring Hill campaign stop
evidence.quote: I think the state should lead in establishing a framework for looking at these [data centers], but I think ultimately you want it to be locally controlled
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports data centers with local control and a state evaluation framework; the article adds he is not opposed to all data centers.

evidence.title: Local 3 News: Data centers and Flock cameras, what the GOP candidates for governor think
evidence.quote: For Tennessee, I think this should be a local decision. I think local communities should have the final say on what happens in their communities.
evidence.what_it_shows: His core position: local say, no state-level block.

evidence.title: Local 3 News: Rose on Chinese interference in data center fights
evidence.quote: there's sufficient evidence now that the Chinese are actually interfering in the affairs of our country. They're actually spending money to try to stir up dissent here at home
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts local opposition to data centers as partly China-driven and argues the US must host AI computing itself, a pro-build framing.

ai_risk.summary: No position found on AI safety rules, chatbots, deepfakes or liability as of Sept 2026. His only AI remarks came inside data center answers, arguing the US must not depend on China to power artificial intelligence.

evidence.title: Local 3 News: Rose on AI and China in data center answer
evidence.quote: We certainly don't want to be dependent on China for powering things like artificial intelligence because we can easily see a country that's our sworn enemy how they would use that power
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI as a national security race with China, but says nothing about safety rules for AI itself.

tech_regulation.summary: Targeted rules. He called TikTok a clear and present danger and voted for the divestiture law, cosponsored the House Kids Online Safety Act and the SCREEN Act, backed a ban on new DJI drones, voted for the 2022 antitrust filing-fee package, and wrote a homebuyer credit-data privacy law that Trump signed in 2025.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Rose floor speech, TikTok currently poses clear and present danger to the United States
evidence.quote: TikTok currently poses an undoubtedly clear and present danger to the United States and its users across the country.
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports forcing foreign-adversary control out of a major app.

evidence.title: Roll call 86 (Mar 13, 2024), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok): Rose Yea
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted for the TikTok divestiture bill.

evidence.title: H.R. 7891, Kids Online Safety Act (House version, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a duty on platforms to protect kids.

evidence.title: H.R. 1623, SCREEN Act (age verification for adult websites)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a specific kids online safety rule.

evidence.title: H.R. 2864, Countering CCP Drones Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports restricting Chinese-made tech over spying concerns.

evidence.title: Rose website reposts Daily Signal article: with GOP support, House takes first big step to curb power of Big Tech
evidence.what_it_shows: His office highlights that he was one of 39 House Republicans who voted for the 2022 antitrust package aimed at Big Tech.

evidence.title: Press release: President Trump signs Rep. Rose's bill to safeguard homebuyer privacy into law
evidence.what_it_shows: A narrow consumer data privacy law he authored, consistent with targeted fixes rather than broad tech regulation.

preemption.summary: No statement found on the state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order or the Mar 2026 White House preemption framework. His 'local decision' stance on data centers is about zoning, not AI law preemption.

china_chips.summary: No position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. He is a China hawk on TikTok, drones and data center siting, but none of that addresses semiconductor exports.

search_notes: About 12 searches (AI, data centers, financial services AI, China/chips, Big Tech/KOSA, preemption, governor race data centers, Quiver releases, Anthropic PAC) plus a Wayback listing of johnrose.house.gov. Opened: Williamson Scene (Jul 22 2026), Local 3 News candidates piece (Jul 24 2026), Nashville Banner 30-question survey (no data center or AI questions), WSMV candidate roundup (no data center answers from Rose), his TikTok, Big Tech and homebuyer privacy releases, govtrack roll call 86. The state file's leads about questioning Hegseth on Anthropic and holding SASC cyber subcommittee leadership were actually Sen. Jacky Rosen (verified at The Verge) and were discarded. Rose sits on the Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence but no AI hearing remarks were found. Headline-only context: he lost the Aug 6, 2026 GOP gubernatorial primary to Blackburn and conceded; Johnny Garrett won the GOP nomination for his House seat; Tennessee Lookout reported Anthropic gave $250K to a pro-Blackburn PAC in the primary's last days (not opened, about his opponent). Local 3 and WBIR interview pages blocked (429/403).

name: Matt Van Epps
signature: Freshman on the Science Committee who champions Trump's AI, quantum and nuclear agenda, wants US open-weight models to counter Chinese distillation, and sponsors the Web of Biological Data Act.

notable_quote.text: We must maintain the lead across the board when it comes to AI.

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on data centers, TVA rates or the Nashville-area moratorium as of Sept 2026. His energy remarks focus on advanced nuclear reactors.

ai_risk.summary: Light touch. In a July 2026 Science Committee hearing he praised the White House National AI Legislative Framework for spurring AI innovation, said America must keep the lead across the board on AI, and treated lighter guardrails on open-weight models as a competitiveness issue rather than a safety problem. He also cosponsored the NSF AI Education Act.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Van Epps speaks at SST budget hearing on revitalizing American scientific research (opening remarks)
evidence.quote: the National AI Legislative Framework provided clear direction on how Congress should act to spur…on AI innovation that serves Americans
evidence.what_it_shows: Endorses the Trump administration's innovation-first AI framework.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Van Epps questions OSTP Director Kratsios on AI leadership
evidence.quote: US companies are turning toward open-source and open-weight models as they are cheaper, customizable, and… have less guardrails.
evidence.what_it_shows: He notes weaker guardrails on open models as a fact of the market and asks how to protect US leadership, not how to add safety rules.

evidence.title: H.R. 5351, NSF AI Education Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports growing the AI workforce, a pro-adoption measure.

tech_regulation.summary: No statements or bills found on Big Tech, Section 230, kids online safety or privacy as of Sept 2026. He joined Congress in Dec 2025 and was not present for the 2024 TikTok vote.

preemption.summary: Leans toward one national standard, based only on his praise for the White House National AI Legislative Framework, which calls for preempting state AI laws. He has not spoken about preemption directly.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Van Epps speaks at SST budget hearing (opening remarks praising OSTP)
evidence.quote: the National AI Legislative Framework provided clear direction on how Congress should act to spur…on AI innovation that serves Americans
evidence.what_it_shows: Endorses the March 2026 White House framework, whose centerpiece is a single federal AI rulebook over state laws, though he does not mention preemption itself.

china_chips.summary: Leans hawkish on Chinese AI: he pressed the White House on the threat from Chinese open-weight models and covert distillation of American models, and cosponsored a bill having the State Department assess foreign adversary AI. No statement found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Van Epps questions OSTP Director Kratsios on Chinese open-weight models
evidence.quote: how is OSTP responding to the threat to American AI leadership posed by Chinese open source and open weight models?
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats Chinese AI models and distillation of US models as a threat to counter.

evidence.title: H.R. 7058, Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a formal assessment of dangers from AI built by rival countries such as China.

search_notes: About 9 searches (AI, data centers, China/chips/TikTok, chatbot/social media/TVA/energy, biological data bill, Quiver releases, Clarksville Now) plus Wayback listings of vanepps.house.gov. Opened: his Jul 23, 2026 SST hearing press release (verbatim remarks and questions), his Dec 2025 committee assignment release, Quiver summaries of the hearing release and his Jul 2026 NDAA amendments (defense tech fielding, Fort Campbell), and the press release listing on his site. Google News link decoding was rate-limited, so the Clarksville Now story on the Web of Biological Data Act (with Auchincloss and Young), the Ripon Advance version, and a NewsChannel 5 interview were not opened. He has been in office only since Dec 4, 2025, so the record is thin. Nothing found on data centers, preemption directly, kids online safety or chip export controls.

name: David Kustoff
signature: Low profile on AI: welcomed xAI's Memphis supercomputer as a historic investment in 2024, cosponsored the NO FAKES Act and the Connected Vehicle Security Act, and voted for the TikTok divestiture law.

notable_quote.text: This historic investment, which is the largest single investment in Memphis’ history, will lead us into the next generation of technology and transform West Tennessee into an innovation hub

data_centers.summary: Celebrated xAI's Memphis supercomputer in June 2024 as a historic investment that would make West Tennessee an innovation hub, and praised grid investment to meet growing demand. No statements found since on the turbine, water or TVA rate fights, so this rests on one early post.

evidence.title: Commercial Appeal: Memphis political leaders react to xAI supercomputer (Kustoff post on X)
evidence.quote: This historic investment, which is the largest single investment in Memphis’ history, will lead us into the next generation of technology and transform West Tennessee into an innovation hub
evidence.what_it_shows: Unconditional welcome for the region's biggest AI data center project.

evidence.title: Press release: Kustoff statement on Hitachi Energy investment in Crockett County
evidence.quote: this project strengthens our nation’s energy infrastructure and ensures grid stability as we meet growing energy demand
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames rising power demand as something to build for, not restrain.

ai_risk.summary: Leans toward targeted guardrails based on one bill: he cosponsored the 2024 NO FAKES Act giving people the right to block AI copies of their voice and face. No statements found on AI safety, chatbots or liability.

evidence.title: H.R. 9551, NO FAKES Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a specific rule against unauthorized AI deepfakes of real people.

tech_regulation.summary: Targeted rules, mostly China-focused: cosponsor of the Connected Vehicle Security Act banning Chinese-linked car software, voted for the TikTok divestiture bill, and cosponsored NO FAKES. No broad Big Tech, antitrust or Section 230 positions found.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning connected-car tech tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Roll call 86 (Mar 13, 2024), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok): Kustoff Yea
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to force TikTok's divestiture from Chinese control.

evidence.title: H.R. 9551, NO FAKES Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a likeness-rights rule aimed at AI platforms.

preemption.summary: No statement found on the state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order or the Mar 2026 White House framework as of Sept 2026.

china_chips.summary: No position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China. His China-tech record (TikTok vote, connected vehicles) does not touch semiconductors.

search_notes: About 9 searches (AI, data centers/xAI, Big Tech/TikTok/deepfake, NO FAKES/crypto/connected vehicles, Section 230/Ways and Means, Quiver releases, xAI Memphis 2025-26, turbines/Boxtown/TVA, TikTok vote) plus a Wayback listing and the live press release page of kustoff.house.gov. name: Steve Cohen
groups: Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus (member; listed by landscape pass, membership page could not be opened)
signature: Tennessee's most active member on data centers: sponsor of the Clean Cloud Act, original cosponsor of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, and author of repeated letters pressing xAI on Memphis turbine pollution; retiring in Jan 2027 after redistricting.

notable_quote.text: We cannot allow high-demand industries to increase pressure on the Tennessee Valley Authority’s (TVA) system or lead to higher bills for Memphis households.

data_centers.summary: He welcomed xAI's Memphis supercomputer in 2024, then turned sharply critical: he sponsored the Clean Cloud Act, cosponsored five more data center bills including the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, and wrote repeatedly demanding the strictest emissions controls, transparency and ratepayer protection from xAI. His own words stress conditions rather than blocking, but the moratorium cosponsorship puts him in the pause camp.

evidence.title: H.R. 9442, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a temporary national stop on new AI data centers until their effects on bills and the environment are sorted out.

evidence.title: H.R. 6179, Clean Cloud Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill sets pollution limits and fees on power used by big data centers and crypto mines.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Cohen introduces the Clean Cloud Act
evidence.quote: We cannot allow high-demand industries to increase pressure on the Tennessee Valley Authority’s (TVA) system or lead to higher bills for Memphis households.
evidence.what_it_shows: Puts ratepayers and the grid ahead of data center growth.

evidence.title: Press release: Cohen submits public comment on xAI emissions permit to Shelby County Health Department
evidence.quote: I support the strictest emissions requirements because I am concerned about the potential cumulative impact on health that the natural gas-powered turbines may have on the neighboring communities
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants the toughest pollution controls, monitoring and site visits on xAI's gas turbines.

evidence.title: Press release: Cohen seeks greater transparency from xAI on its power generation impact on public health
evidence.quote: I understand the transformative economic potential of data centers. However, any largescale development, especially those involving significant energy consumption and onsite combustion sources, warrant early, transparent, and ongoing engagement with surrounding communities.
evidence.what_it_shows: Acknowledges economic upside but demands transparency and community engagement; a conditions-first stance.

evidence.title: Press release: Cohen urges immediate continuation of Colossus water recycling plant construction
evidence.quote: The Memphis Sand Aquifer is one of our most vital resources and must be protected.
evidence.what_it_shows: Presses xAI to keep its water commitments to the community.

evidence.title: H.R. 6529, Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs keeping families' electric bills from paying for data center grid costs.

evidence.title: H.R. 7858, Data Center Community Impact Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires builders to show impacts on local power, water and bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 8488, AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: More public disclosure before data centers are sited.

evidence.title: H.R. 9183, Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Government study and voluntary reporting of AI's energy, water and pollution footprint.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Cohen applauds economic impact of xAI Gigafactory in Memphis
evidence.quote: This is great news for Memphis and the Memphis economy and will make our region a focus for the future of artificial intelligence.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory early evidence: he cheered the project before the turbine and water fights.

ai_risk.summary: Targeted guardrails. He cosponsored the Algorithmic Accountability Act in both the 118th and 119th Congresses, the Algorithmic Justice and Online Platform Transparency Act, the resolution blocking Medicare's AI prior-authorization experiment, and a bill letting musicians bargain with AI companies. No calls for licensing or a pause were found.

evidence.title: H.R. 5511, Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report to the FTC.

evidence.title: H.R. 5628, Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Repeat support across two Congresses for AI impact assessments.

evidence.title: H.J.Res. 187, disapproving the CMS WISeR rule (AI prior authorization in Medicare)
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes letting contractors use AI to gate medical treatments.

evidence.title: H.R. 4624, Algorithmic Justice and Online Platform Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make platforms explain their algorithms and ban discriminatory ones.

evidence.title: H.R. 8994, Protect Working Musicians Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets small musicians collectively bargain with or refuse AI companies using their work.

tech_regulation.summary: Targeted rules: voted for the TikTok divestiture bill, cosponsored the Connected Vehicle Security Act, the My Body, My Data Act on reproductive health data, and the Algorithmic Justice and Online Platform Transparency Act. No break-up or Section 230 repeal positions found.

evidence.title: Roll call 86 (Mar 13, 2024), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok): Cohen Yea
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to force TikTok's divestiture from Chinese control.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730, Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs banning connected-car tech tied to adversary nations.

evidence.title: H.R. 3420, My Body, My Data Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports privacy limits on reproductive health data collection.

evidence.title: H.R. 4624, Algorithmic Justice and Online Platform Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Platform transparency and anti-discrimination rules.

preemption.summary: Let states regulate. He signed the Dec 3, 2025 Clarke letter from 44 House Democrats urging that no AI moratorium or preemption of state AI laws be put in the FY26 defense bill.

evidence.title: Clarke-led House Democratic letter to Armed Services leaders opposing any AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Cohen listed as signer)

evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on to oppose federal preemption or a moratorium on state AI laws.

china_chips.summary: Cosponsored the Chip Security Act, which would require location tracking on advanced AI chips to catch smuggling to China. No statements found on Nvidia H20/H200 sales.

evidence.title: H.R. 3447, Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports tighter enforcement of chip export controls.
